question: Identify the function of the enzyme trypsin.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Digesting Proteins.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trypsin**

 
 
• **​**The function of the enzyme **trypsin** is** to digest proteins**.
 
• By breaking up lengthy chains of** amino acids** into smaller pieces, the enzyme trypsin in the early part of the small intestine initiates the breakdown of **protein **molecules.
 
• It is a serine protease from the PA clan superfamily that **hydrolyzes proteins** in the digestive tracts of numerous animals.
 
• When the **pancreatic** **enzyme **trypsinogen, in the proenzyme form, is activated, **trypsin **is generated in the **small intestine**.
 
• The **carboxyl** side of the amino acids lysine or arginine is where trypsin primarily breaks peptide chains. It is employed in a variety of **biotechnological procedures**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One significant** protease, trypsin**, has the unique ability to **catalyze** the **hydrolysis** of **peptide** and **ester** **bonds** with **lysine** and arginine amino acids at the **carboxyl-terminus.**
 
• Additionally, an autocatalytic, trypsin produces additional trypsin by converting **trypsinogen**.
 
• In addition to its basic function of breaking down dietary protein, trypsin also transforms the other two zymogens into **chymotrypsin and carboxypeptidase.**
